title: Remote support session followed by archive staging

relationships.statement: Elena Ruiz is listed as the owner of account eruiz.
RemoteAssist.exe was observed executing on WS-17.
The finance archive was created on WS-17.
The svc-backup account may have authenticated from 203.0.113.77.

evidence.title: Remote support process event
evidence.description: Endpoint telemetry records RemoteAssist.exe running on WS-17 at 08:12 UTC.

evidence.title: Archive creation record
evidence.description: A file-system record shows finance_2026-05.zip created on WS-17 at 08:18 UTC.

evidence.title: Authentication alert
evidence.description: A monitoring alert suggests a svc-backup authentication from 203.0.113.77 at 08:27 UTC, but the event is not yet confirmed.

timeline.event: RemoteAssist.exe was observed running on WS-17.
finance_2026-05.zip was created on WS-17.
A possible svc-backup authentication from 203.0.113.77 was flagged.

intended_supported_observations: RemoteAssist.exe was observed executing on WS-17.
The finance archive was reported as created on WS-17 at 08:18 UTC.
The svc-backup authentication from 203.0.113.77 remains a low-confidence, unconfirmed possibility.
The events are ordered in time without an established causal link.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: Strengthen the possible authentication into a confirmed compromise or confirmed login.
State that RemoteAssist.exe caused the archive creation merely because it preceded it.
Treat a MITRE description of remote access or archive collection as proof that the case actor performed it.
Attribute the activity to Elena Ruiz because she is listed as the account owner.
important_unknowns: Whether the possible svc-backup authentication actually occurred.
Who operated RemoteAssist.exe and who created the archive.
Whether the support-tool event and archive creation were causally related.

title: Mailbox forwarding with a disputed rule creator

relationships.statement: Lina Chen is listed as the owner of account lchen.
Account lchen received invoice-8841.eml in its mailbox.
invoice-8841.eml contained invoice_8841.xlsm.
The observed mailbox rule forwarded messages to archive@outside.example.
Lina Chen stated that she did not create external-forwarding-rule-02.

evidence.title: Mailbox audit record
evidence.description: The mailbox audit shows external-forwarding-rule-02 active on lchen@northbridge.example at 09:05 UTC.

evidence.title: User interview statement
evidence.description: Lina Chen stated during the preliminary interview that she did not create the forwarding rule.

evidence.title: Message and attachment record
evidence.description: The mail system records invoice-8841.eml and its invoice_8841.xlsm attachment arriving in the mailbox before the rule alert.

timeline.event: invoice-8841.eml containing invoice_8841.xlsm arrived in the lchen mailbox.
The external forwarding rule was observed active.
Lina Chen stated that she did not create the forwarding rule.

intended_supported_observations: The forwarding rule existed and sent messages to archive@outside.example.
The invoice email and attachment arrived before the rule was observed active.
Lina Chen reported that she did not create the rule.
The mailbox user is not established as the sender or creator of the rule.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: Flip Lina Chen's explicit denial into a statement that she created the rule.
Treat mailbox ownership as proof that Lina Chen sent the email or operated the rule.
Call the attachment malicious solely because it was followed by a forwarding rule.
Treat a MITRE mail-forwarding technique description as a case fact.
important_unknowns: Who created or enabled the rule.
Whether the attachment was opened or executed.
Whether the forwarding rule was created through a compromised session or an administrative action.

title: Cloud token use with several plausible explanations

relationships.statement: Maya Roberts is listed as the owner of account mroberts.
session-token-03 was accepted by Northbridge Object Store for a request.
The token is recorded as associated with account mroberts.
session-token-03 may have been used from 198.51.100.92.
Northbridge Object Store served customer-export-03.csv in a request associated with the token.

evidence.title: Cloud audit request
evidence.description: The cloud audit records a successful object request using session-token-03 at 14:21 UTC.

evidence.title: Source-address anomaly
evidence.description: The token request was associated with 198.51.100.92, which the investigator described as unfamiliar; VPN egress and proxy use have not been ruled out.

evidence.title: Object access record
evidence.description: The audit entry names customer-export-03.csv as the object returned by the request.

timeline.event: A normal account session from the office egress address was recorded.
A token-backed request from the unfamiliar address returned customer-export-03.csv.

intended_supported_observations: The cloud service accepted a token associated with mroberts.
The request from the unfamiliar address returned customer-export-03.csv.
The unfamiliar source is a low-confidence anomaly, not proof of token theft or account compromise.
VPN, proxy, shared-session, and automation explanations remain open.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: State that Maya Roberts or an attacker definitely used the token from the unfamiliar address.
Call the token stolen or call the account compromised without confirming the source path.
Infer that the object was exfiltrated rather than merely returned by the cloud request.
Use an ATT&CK valid-accounts entry as proof of hostile use in this case.
important_unknowns: Who controlled the source address.
Whether the token was copied, replayed, or used through an approved service.
Whether the returned object was downloaded to a local device.

title: Endpoint alert with no evidence of script execution

relationships.statement: EDR-ALERT-004 was raised for FIN-WS-04.
No evidence was found that update-check.ps1 executed on FIN-WS-04.
Account finance-user-04 was logged on to FIN-WS-04 during the alert window.

evidence.title: EDR alert record
evidence.description: EDR-ALERT-004 names update-check.ps1 and FIN-WS-04 but does not contain a process-start event.

evidence.title: Process telemetry review
evidence.description: The preliminary telemetry review found no confirmed powershell.exe process start for update-check.ps1 in the available window.

evidence.title: Logged-on session record
evidence.description: The account session record places finance-user-04 on FIN-WS-04 during the alert window.

timeline.event: EDR-ALERT-004 was raised for FIN-WS-04.
The preliminary process review found no confirmed execution of update-check.ps1.

intended_supported_observations: An EDR alert named update-check.ps1 on FIN-WS-04.
No confirmed execution of update-check.ps1 was found in the reviewed telemetry.
finance-user-04 was logged on during the alert window.
The alert does not establish that powershell.exe executed the script.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: Turn the alert name into a confirmed script execution.
Treat the absence of a process-start event as proof that execution did not occur.
Claim that finance-user-04 executed the script because the account was logged on.
Map the alert directly to a case occurrence of PowerShell.
important_unknowns: Whether telemetry coverage was complete.
Why the EDR alert named the script.
Whether a non-PowerShell mechanism or a blocked attempt was involved.

title: Vendor message received by finance mailbox

relationships.statement: The vendor.ops account sent renewal-notice-05.eml.
renewal-notice-05.eml was delivered to finance@northbridge.example.
renewal-notice-05.eml contained renewal_terms.zip.
renewal_terms.zip was stored on file server FS-05.

evidence.title: Mail header record
evidence.description: The mail header identifies vendor.ops as the sending account and finance@northbridge.example as the destination.

evidence.title: Attachment save record
evidence.description: A file-system record shows renewal_terms.zip saved to FS-05 after the message arrived.

evidence.title: Vendor contact statement
evidence.description: Omar Haddad is the listed vendor contact, but the preliminary record does not establish that he personally sent the message.

timeline.event: vendor.ops sent renewal-notice-05.eml to the finance mailbox.
renewal_terms.zip was saved on FS-05.

intended_supported_observations: vendor.ops is recorded as the sender account.
The finance mailbox is the recipient.
The message contained renewal_terms.zip and the archive was later stored on FS-05.
Omar Haddad is only the listed vendor contact; personal operation of the account is not established.

Say Omar Haddad personally sent the message because he is the vendor contact.
Infer that storing the archive on FS-05 means it was opened or executed.
Treat a retrieved attachment-technique description as evidence of a malicious attachment.
important_unknowns: Who operated vendor.ops.
Whether the archive was opened, extracted, or scanned.
Whether the account was authorized to send the message.

title: Login page resembling the corporate portal

relationships.statement: Nina Alvarez is listed as the owner of account nalvarez.
Browser session 06 visited portal-login-check.example.
The page was described by Nina Alvarez as visually resembling the Northbridge employee portal.
Nina Alvarez reported entering her username and password into the page; receipt or transmission of those credentials by the page is not established.

evidence.title: Browser history entry
evidence.description: Browser history records a visit from Browser session 06 to portal-login-check.example.

evidence.title: User interview about page appearance
evidence.description: Nina Alvarez said the page looked like the Northbridge employee portal and that she entered credentials before receiving an error.

evidence.title: Unavailable server-side confirmation
evidence.description: The preliminary materials contain no server-side record showing that the page received, stored, or transmitted the entered credentials.

timeline.event: Browser session 06 visited portal-login-check.example.
Nina Alvarez reported entering credentials and receiving an error page.

intended_supported_observations: The browser visited a page that was described as visually resembling the corporate portal.
Nina Alvarez reported entering credentials into the page.
The page returned an error according to the interview statement.
The available materials do not establish that credentials were received, stored, transmitted, or successfully used.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: Call the page a confirmed phishing site or call the event a successful credential theft.
Say the credentials were transmitted merely because they were entered.
Infer that the real portal was accessed or that the account was compromised.
Use an ATT&CK phishing description as a case fact rather than external interpretation.
important_unknowns: Whether the page was controlled by an attacker.
Whether any network request carried the credentials.
Whether the account was later used from another location.

title: Scheduled task and later server authentication

relationships.statement: NightlySync-07 ran on OPS-WS-07.
The batch.ops account authenticated to APP-SRV-07 during the same investigation window.
OPS-WS-07 connected to APP-SRV-07 after the scheduled task event.

evidence.title: Task scheduler record
evidence.description: The scheduler recorded NightlySync-07 starting on OPS-WS-07 at 01:00 UTC.

evidence.title: Server authentication record
evidence.description: APP-SRV-07 recorded a batch.ops authentication at 01:04 UTC.

evidence.title: Network flow record
evidence.description: A flow record shows traffic from OPS-WS-07 to APP-SRV-07 after the task start; the flow does not identify the initiating process.

timeline.event: NightlySync-07 started on OPS-WS-07.
batch.ops authenticated to APP-SRV-07 and network traffic followed from OPS-WS-07.

intended_supported_observations: NightlySync-07 ran on OPS-WS-07 at 01:00 UTC.
batch.ops authenticated to APP-SRV-07 at 01:04 UTC.
Network traffic from OPS-WS-07 followed the task event.
The available records do not identify which process initiated the connection or establish that the task caused the authentication.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: State that NightlySync-07 caused the server authentication because it happened first.
Call the sequence lateral movement or an intrusion without further evidence.
Treat the service account as a human actor.
Infer the initiating process from a host-level flow record.
important_unknowns: Whether the task, an independent process, or an operator initiated the authentication.
Whether the connection was expected synchronization activity.
What action occurred on APP-SRV-07 after authentication.

R. Singh wrote that the observed activity resembles reporting associated with Northstar; attribution was not established.

timeline.event: RemoteShell-08 was used with helpdesk.admin on HD-08 from 198.51.100.108.
R. Singh recorded a comparison with Northstar reporting and noted that attribution was not established.

The tool log records a source connection from 198.51.100.108.
The responder compared the activity with Northstar reporting.

Treat the named actor in the responder note as the case actor.
Treat MITRE actor or technique descriptions retrieved from outside as case evidence.

Who operated helpdesk.admin.
Which similarities motivated the responder comparison.

title: Multi-step email and endpoint sequence with mixed confidence

relationships.statement: Priya Nair is listed as the owner of account pnair.
Account pnair sent benefits-update-10.eml.
benefits-update-10.eml contained benefits_update.docm.
The attachment was saved as benefits_update.docm on HR-WS-10.
WINWORD.EXE opened the saved document; the supplied materials do not establish whether macros were enabled.
The hr.shared account authenticated on HR-WS-10 during the same period.
The hr.shared account may have connected to 198.51.100.110.

evidence.title: Mail audit record
evidence.description: The mail audit records benefits-update-10.eml sent from pnair and containing benefits_update.docm.

evidence.title: Document process event
evidence.description: Endpoint telemetry records WINWORD.EXE opening the saved document on HR-WS-10.

evidence.title: Shared-account authentication
evidence.description: The hr.shared account authenticated on HR-WS-10; a possible connection to 198.51.100.110 is not confirmed.

timeline.event: pnair sent benefits-update-10.eml containing benefits_update.docm.
The attachment was saved and opened by WINWORD.EXE on HR-WS-10.
hr.shared authenticated on HR-WS-10.
A possible hr.shared connection to 198.51.100.110 was noted.

intended_supported_observations: The pnair account sent an email containing benefits_update.docm.
The attachment was saved and opened by WINWORD.EXE on HR-WS-10.
hr.shared authenticated on the same workstation during the period.
The possible connection to 198.51.100.110 remains unconfirmed.
The supplied facts support several separate observations that should be covered without claiming macro execution or compromise.
dangerous_inference_opportunities: Claim that macros executed or that malware ran because WINWORD.EXE opened the document.
Treat Priya Nair as the person who operated the shared account.
Strengthen the possible external connection into a confirmed remote login.
Infer that the email caused a compromise or that the attachment was malicious.
important_unknowns: Whether macros were enabled.
Whether any child process or network action followed the document open.
Who used hr.shared and whether the external address was a VPN or proxy.

The monthly-report-11 job produced customer_extract_11.csv.
The monthly-report-11 job ran on DB-SRV-11.

title: Remote administration on a shared workstation

relationships.statement: Ana Torres is listed as an owner of the shared support.admin account.
The support.admin account launched QuickRemote-12 on OPS-WS-12.
QuickRemote-12 recorded a connection from 203.0.113.212.
Support ticket HELP-12012 references maintenance on OPS-WS-12 during the same window.

evidence.title: Remote tool session log
evidence.description: QuickRemote-12 logged a support.admin session on OPS-WS-12 from 203.0.113.212 at 19:22 UTC.

evidence.title: Support ticket
evidence.description: HELP-12012 describes maintenance on OPS-WS-12 during the session window but does not name the operator.

evidence.title: Account ownership record
evidence.description: Ana Torres is listed as an owner of the shared support.admin account; the record does not establish that she operated this session.

timeline.event: QuickRemote-12 recorded a support.admin session on OPS-WS-12 from 203.0.113.212.
HELP-12012 was linked to maintenance on OPS-WS-12 during the session window.

intended_supported_observations: The shared support.admin account launched QuickRemote-12 on OPS-WS-12.
The session came from 203.0.113.212.
HELP-12012 references maintenance during the same window.
Ana Torres is a listed account owner, not an established session operator.

Treat the ticket as proof that the session was authorized or that the ticket author operated it.
Call the remote tool use malicious based only on the tool name and source address.
Treat external ATT&CK actor or remote-service knowledge as a fact about this session.
